page: Amazon Web Services gr6.8xlarge is a graphics-intensive server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores running at 3.4 GHz, paired with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz. This configuration establishes a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio. For acceleration, the instance includes a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing 22 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided via a 900 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity features a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in specific workloads. The single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is in the top 25%, while multi-core performance sits in the middle 50%. The instance demonstrates top-tier capabilities in LLM inference for small and medium models, both in prompt processing and text generation. Image processing and CPU encryption benchmarks also rank in the top 25%. However, standard memory bandwidth and multi-core integer or decompression tasks perform in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, the gr6.8xlarge offers a balanced profile for workloads requiring both GPU acceleration and a high memory-to-vCPU ratio. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage and dedicated CPU allocation supports consistent I/O performance. This instance is suited for graphics-intensive applications, machine learning inference, image processing, and database operations that benefit from GPU acceleration and substantial memory capacity.
